hints.title: Session Duration Rounding
hints.text: For each session in Logs, compute the duration in seconds and round up to the nearest minute using the ceiling function.

hints.title: Left Join All Employees
hints.text: Join Employees with Logs using a left join so that employees with zero recorded sessions are retained with zero total minutes.

hints.title: Deduction Threshold Comparison
hints.text: Group by employee id and filter for employees whose summed logged minutes are strictly less than their required hours multiplied by 60.

hints.title: Group Filter Query Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
select
    e.employee_id
from Employees e
left join Logs l on e.employee_id = l.employee_id
group by e.employee_id, e.needed_hours
having coalesce(sum(ceil(timestampdiff(second, l.in_time, l.out_time) / 60.0)), 0) < e.needed_hours * 60;
```

complexity.notes: Hash join and single-pass aggregation over employee logs.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated scalar subqueries scanning the logs per employee cause quadratic overhead.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Grouping by employee aggregates minutes directly in memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Properly accounts for ceiling rounding per session and handles employees with no activity via left join.

solutions.approach: Left Join Aggregation with Ceiling Rounding and Having Filter
solutions.code:
select
    e.employee_id
from Employees e
left join Logs l on e.employee_id = l.employee_id
group by e.employee_id, e.needed_hours
having coalesce(sum(ceil(extract(epoch from (l.out_time - l.in_time)) / 60.0)), 0) < e.needed_hours * 60;

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def employees_with_deductions(employees: pd.DataFrame, logs: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    if logs.empty:
        return employees[['employee_id']]
    
    logs_copy = logs.copy()
    diff_sec = (pd.to_datetime(logs_copy['out_time']) - pd.to_datetime(logs_copy['in_time'])).dt.total_seconds()
    logs_copy['minutes'] = np.ceil(diff_sec / 60.0)
    
    worked = logs_copy.groupby('employee_id')['minutes'].sum().reset_index()
    merged = employees.merge(worked, on='employee_id', how='left')
    merged['minutes'] = merged['minutes'].fillna(0)
    
    res = merged[merged['minutes'] < merged['needed_hours'] * 60]
    return res[['employee_id']]
